imports: pytestmark = [pytest.mark.extension_native, pytest.mark.extension_occlusion, pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform != 'win32', reason='Requires the owned Windows native occlusion fixture')]

scenarios.name: real_extension_window_restore_and_hidden_input
scenarios.title: Restore an owned Chrome window and withhold input under real native occlusion
scenarios.workflow: Connect and inspect actual bridge runtime -> minimize and restore the owned window -> activate an inactive owned tab -> focus a normal unfocused window -> cover only the owned window -> refuse mouse and keyboard with separate tab/window/document diagnostics -> uncover -> submit once with trusted input -> inspect final screenshot and preserve unrelated tabs
scenarios.user_problem: An ordinary profile must support window controls and preserve an actionable hidden-page refusal without claiming that native focus proves visibility.
